description: MOQT variable-length integers as specified in draft-ietf-moq-transport-20 §1.4.1. The number of leading 1 bits in the first byte is the encoded length minus one (1 to 9 bytes); the remaining bits of the first byte and every following byte carry the value in network byte order. This is MOQT's own scheme, not the RFC 9000 QUIC varint.
sources: minimal: the examples in draft-ietf-moq-transport-20 §1.4.1 Table 2, plus the smallest and largest value of each encoded length derived from the encoding rules
nonMinimal: the two-byte encoding of 37 from draft-ietf-moq-transport-20 §1.4.1 Table 2, plus zero at longer lengths
beyond53Bits: derived; values above 2^53-1 exercise implementations without exact 64-bit integers
